claims.text: A small, controlled Al addition to CoCrFeNi enhances high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Al addition promotes selective surface segregation of Cr and Al at high temperatures.
Selective Cr and Al enrichment drives formation of a continuous, dense Cr/Al-rich oxide layer.
A continuous, dense Cr/Al-rich oxide layer retards further oxidation.
Elevated temperature enhances atomic diffusion that promotes surface segregation of Cr and Al.
Surface enrichment in Cr and Al triggers formation of an oxide scale predominantly comprising Cr2O3, Al2O3, or mixed Cr/Al-rich phases.
The Cr/Al-rich oxide scale adheres strongly to the alloy substrate.
The Al-containing variant will begin forming a protective oxide scale earlier than the Al-free CoCrFeNi baseline.
The Al-containing variant will form a more uniform and adherent oxide scale than the Al-free baseline.
The Al-containing variant will exhibit lower oxidation-associated weight gain than the Al-free baseline.
The oxide scale on the Al-containing variant will resist spallation better than the oxide scale on the Al-free baseline.
Al-free CoCrFeNi is expected to form a less uniform oxide layer under otherwise equivalent oxidation conditions.
Al-free CoCrFeNi is expected to form a less adherent oxide layer under otherwise equivalent oxidation conditions.
Al-free CoCrFeNi is expected to undergo greater weight gain and more rapid oxidation degradation than the Al-containing variant.
The proposed behavior applies in air between 900 and 1100 °C when the Al addition does not disrupt overall phase stability.
Compositional gradients or inhomogeneities may limit the proposed oxidation mechanism.
Changes in atmospheric oxygen partial pressure may significantly alter oxidation kinetics.
Prior studies suggest that minor Al additions can promote protective oxidation.
The magnitude of the oxidation-resistance benefit from Al addition may depend on the alloy system.
